chapter_title: Ethers and Epoxides; Thiols and Sulfides

questions.chapter_title: Ethers and Epoxides; Thiols and Sulfides
questions.question: In the context of Ethers and Epoxides; Thiols and Sulfides, what is the major organic product when Sodium ethoxide (CH₃CH₂ONa) reacts under the following conditions: CH₃I in acetone?
questions.explanation: Major product rationale: Classic SN2 displacement of iodide by an unhindered alkoxide nucleophile. The correct major product is 'Diethyl ether (CH₃CH₂OCH₃) + NaI'.

questions.chapter_title: Ethers and Epoxides; Thiols and Sulfides
questions.question: In the context of Ethers and Epoxides; Thiols and Sulfides, what is the major organic product when Sodium ethoxide reacts under the following conditions: (CH₃)₃C-Br in EtOH?
questions.explanation: Major product rationale: Steric hindrance on tertiary alkyl halide prevents SN2 substitution; strong alkoxide base undergoes E2 elimination. The correct major product is '2-Methylpropene (Isobutylene) + EtOH + NaBr (E2 exclusively)'.

questions.chapter_title: Ethers and Epoxides; Thiols and Sulfides
questions.question: In the context of Ethers and Epoxides; Thiols and Sulfides, what is the major organic product when CH₃CH₂-O-CH₂CH₃ reacts under the following conditions: Excess HI (conc.), 100°C?
questions.explanation: Major product rationale: Protonation followed by sequential SN2 displacements with iodide cleaves both ether C-O bonds. The correct major product is '2 CH₃CH₂I + H₂O'.

questions.chapter_title: Ethers and Epoxides; Thiols and Sulfides
questions.question: In the context of Ethers and Epoxides; Thiols and Sulfides, what is the major organic product when Cyclohexene reacts under the following conditions: mCPBA / anhydrous CH₂Cl₂?
questions.explanation: Major product rationale: Concerted peroxy acid oxygen transfer converts the alkene double bond into a three-membered oxirane ring. The correct major product is 'Cyclohexene oxide (1,2-Epoxycyclohexane) + m-Chlorobenzoic acid'.

questions.chapter_title: Ethers and Epoxides; Thiols and Sulfides
questions.question: In the context of Ethers and Epoxides; Thiols and Sulfides, what is the major organic product when 1,2-Epoxypropane (Propylene oxide) reacts under the following conditions: NaOCH₃ in anhydrous CH₃OH?
questions.explanation: Major product rationale: Strong basic nucleophile attacks the less sterically hindered carbon (C1) with inversion. The correct major product is '1-Methoxy-2-propanol (SN2 at less substituted carbon)'.

questions.chapter_title: Ethers and Epoxides; Thiols and Sulfides
questions.question: Which reaction conditions / reagents are required to convert 1,2-Epoxypropane into 2-Methoxy-1-propanol (Major, attack at more substituted carbon) in Ethers and Epoxides; Thiols and Sulfides?
questions.explanation: Reagent selection rationale: The transformation '1,2-Epoxypropane' → '2-Methoxy-1-propanol (Major, attack at more substituted carbon)' specifically requires 'CH₃OH / cat. H₂SO₄ (catalytic)'. Mechanistic basis: Protonated epoxide develops significant partial carbocation character at the more substituted C2, directing nucleophile attack there.

questions.chapter_title: Ethers and Epoxides; Thiols and Sulfides
questions.question: Which reaction conditions / reagents are required to convert KF (insoluble in benzene) into Soluble [K(18-crown-6)]⁺ F⁻ ('Naked' fluoride nucleophile) in Ethers and Epoxides; Thiols and Sulfides?
questions.explanation: Reagent selection rationale: The transformation 'KF (insoluble in benzene)' → 'Soluble [K(18-crown-6)]⁺ F⁻ ('Naked' fluoride nucleophile)' specifically requires '18-Crown-6 in dry Benzene'. Mechanistic basis: 18-Crown-6 encapsulates K⁺ ions, dissolving KF in nonpolar benzene and unleashing highly reactive 'naked' fluoride.

questions.chapter_title: Ethers and Epoxides; Thiols and Sulfides
questions.question: Which reaction conditions / reagents are required to convert 2 CH₃CH₂SH into CH₃CH₂-S-S-CH₂CH₃ (Diethyl disulfide) + 2 HI in Ethers and Epoxides; Thiols and Sulfides?

questions.chapter_title: Ethers and Epoxides; Thiols and Sulfides
questions.question: Which starting material yields '2 CH₃CH₂SH (Ethanethiol)' when treated with 'Zn / aqueous HCl, Δ' according to the principles of Ethers and Epoxides; Thiols and Sulfides?
questions.explanation: Starting material deduction: Treating 'Diethyl disulfide' with 'Zn / aqueous HCl, Δ' yields '2 CH₃CH₂SH (Ethanethiol)'. Mechanistic rationale: Reductive cleavage of the sulfur-sulfur bond regenerates two thiol equivalents.
